issues.legal_issue: A decree and later proceedings procured through fraud on a court are nullities.
material_facts: The owner had sold the property before the municipal tax proceedings but did not disclose the sale to the municipality or the court.
He did not contest the tax suit or execution, despite having the means to pay the tax, and the property was bought at auction by his wife.
The courts below found that he concealed the sale and sent purported notice to the purchaser at a false address.
issues.conclusion: The fraud findings were supported; a decree obtained by fraud is a nullity, as are proceedings taken pursuant to it.
issues.legal_principle: A judgment, decree or order obtained by fraud on a court is a nullity and may be challenged in collateral proceedings. The Court relied on S.P. Chengalvaraya Naidu v. Jagannath, Ram Chandra Singh v. Savitri Devi, Tulsi v. Chandrika Prasad, and A.V. Papayya Sastry v. Government of A.P.

predicates.title_challenge_after_execution_sale: A third party brought a proceeding to challenge title derived from a court execution sale.
predicates.judgment_debtor_concealed_prior_transfer: The judgment-debtor failed to disclose an earlier transfer of the property to the person claiming title.
predicates.judgment_debtor_engineered_or_enabled_pr: The judgment-debtor's conduct enabled the decree or execution sale to proceed without a genuine contest.

issues.definition: When a third party challenges title derived from an execution sale and the judgment-debtor concealed an earlier transfer while enabling the proceedings to go forward, the decree and subsequent proceedings are treated as nullities.

issues.legal_issue: Omission of a decree-holder from a third-party suit challenging the judgment-debtor's title does not entitle an auction purchaser or successor to appellate relief where fraud and the equities of the case weigh against that relief.
material_facts: The original purchaser sued to establish title against the judgment-debtor and persons claiming through the auction purchaser, but did not join the municipality that had obtained the tax decree.

The appellants and their predecessors acquired the property during the title litigation, and the courts found serious fraud by the judgment-debtor and his wife in relation to the earlier sale and auction.
The appellants relied on the decree-holder's non-joinder; the Court assumed, without deciding, that the courts below had been wrong to find that the relevant CPC provision did not apply.
The municipality's right to recover the property tax was not disputed, and the Court directed payment of the amount disbursed to the municipality from the auction proceeds.
issues.conclusion: The Court refused to grant the appellants relief on the basis of non-joinder. Exercising its powers to do complete justice, it directed the respondents to deposit the amount paid to the municipality from the auction proceeds; upon payment, the appeal would stand dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Order XXI, Rule 92(4) CPC makes the decree-holder and judgment-debtor necessary parties to a third-party suit challenging the judgment-debtor's title against an auction purchaser; Rule 92(5) provides for refund by the decree-holder and revival of execution if the suit is decreed. The Court assumed that Rule 92(4) could apply, but relied on its equitable jurisdiction under Articles 136 and 142 of the Constitution to deny relief to the appellants in light of the fraud and the competing rights. It referred to Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan v. Ajay Kumar Das and A. Umarani v. Registrar, Cooperative Societies on the consequences of nullity, and Chandra Singh v. State of Rajasthan and Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Brij Mohan on doing complete justice.

rule.if: appeal_from_third_party_title_suit and decree_holder_not_joined and judgment_debtor_committed_fraud and appellant_claims_through_auction_purchaser and decree_holder_has_unpaid_property_claim

predicates.appeal_from_third_party_title_suit: An appeal arises from a third party's suit challenging title claimed through a court auction purchaser.
predicates.decree_holder_not_joined: The party that obtained the decree under which the property was auctioned was not joined in the third-party suit.
predicates.judgment_debtor_committed_fraud: The judgment-debtor fraudulently concealed an earlier transfer and allowed the decree and auction proceedings to proceed.
predicates.appellant_claims_through_auction_purchas: The appellant claims the property through the purchaser at the challenged execution sale.
predicates.decree_holder_has_unpaid_property_claim: The decree-holder retains a property-related claim for which recovery has not been disputed.

issues.definition: In an appeal from a third-party title suit, when the decree-holder was not joined but the appellant claims through an auction purchaser and the judgment-debtor committed fraud, appellate relief may be denied subject to an equitable condition protecting the decree-holder's unpaid claim.

issues.legal_issue: A statutory charge for property tax remains enforceable against the property, and a transferee liable for tax may redeem that charge by payment.
material_facts: Property tax was unpaid for the relevant period, and the property was sold without the transfer being notified to the municipal authority or recorded in its registers.
The tax decree was obtained by the municipality, which received money from the execution auction.

The municipality's right to recover the tax was not disputed; the respondents accepted liability for tax accruing after the sale, and the Court directed them to pay the amount disbursed to the municipality from the auction proceeds.
issues.conclusion: The respondents were directed to deposit the amount paid to the municipality from the auction proceeds, thereby protecting the municipality's right to recover the tax; the appeal would stand dismissed upon that payment.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 85 and 88 of the Tamil Nadu District Municipalities Act, 1920 make property tax a first charge and continue the transferor's liability when notice of transfer is not given, without displacing the transferee's liability. Section 55(1)(g) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 places tax liability on the vendor up to the sale, while Order XXXIV, Rule 15 CPC and Section 100 of the Transfer of Property Act apply mortgage principles, so far as may be, to a statutory charge and permit its redemption.

predicates.property_tax_unpaid: Property tax assessed on the property remained unpaid.
predicates.property_tax_charge_attaches_to_property: The law governing the property tax makes the tax a charge on the property.
predicates.transfer_not_notified_to_municipal_autho: The transferor and transferee did not notify the municipal authority of the transfer as required.
predicates.transferee_is_liable_for_post_transfer_t: The transferee is liable for property tax arising after the transfer.

issues.definition: When property tax remains unpaid, the tax is charged on the property, the transfer was not notified, and the transferee is liable for later tax, the transferee must pay the tax claim to redeem the charge.

issues.legal_issue: A transferee who acquires property during a pending suit concerning it is bound by the result of that litigation.
material_facts: The original purchaser filed a suit asserting title to the property.
The property was transferred to the appellants and their predecessors while that suit was pending.
The evidence and findings showed that the later purchasers had notice of the earlier sale and the pending suit.
issues.conclusion: The appellants and their predecessors were bound by the decree because they purchased pendente lite, with notice of the prior sale.
issues.legal_principle: Section 52 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 bars a transfer of immovable property during litigation from affecting the rights of the other parties under the decree. Section 3 addresses notice, including notice arising where a transaction affecting immovable property has been effected by a registered instrument. The Court also relied on Mangru Mahto v. Shri Thakur Taraknathji Tarakeshwar Math concerning the effect of a transfer made during mortgage litigation.

predicates.suit_concerning_property_is_pending: A suit concerning rights in the property is pending before a court.
predicates.property_transferred_during_suit: The property is transferred while that suit remains pending.
predicates.transferee_claims_under_that_transfer: The transferee bases a claim to the property on the transfer made during the suit.

issues.definition: When a suit concerning property is pending and a transferee claims under a transfer made during that suit, the transferee is bound by its result.
